The most overs batted by New Zealand in the third or fourth innings to save a Test is 220.3 overs (671/4) against Sri Lanka in 1991, followed by 210 (680/8d) against India in 2014 - both at this venue. These two innings featured the top two individual scores for New Zealand in Tests: Martin Crowe’s 299 in 1991 and Brendon McCullum’s 302 in 2014.
New Zealand batted with a control percentage of 81.6% in the first 30 overs of this innings, 98.9% in the 15 overs thereafter.

Rishabh Pant (1/2): [How do you rank that hundred?] I think definitely it was a good one. New Zealand was one place where I was eyeing that hundred for sure. And I made sure that in a wicket like this where you have to grind and everyone is batting well, I just wanted to stay there as long as possible and just make my impact. [How much of your innings is premeditated?] I think for me, I don't think about that a lot of time. I try to play the bowler's mind most of the time, but like I just keep it simple most of the time whenever I see the ball, I try to hit it. I think that's the, if it's in my area, I'll try to hit it for sure. [How badly did you want to hit a six to bring up your hundred? Was that a plan?] See, mostly whenever I'm trying to get a hundred, I try to get it by six. But because of that, I've also missed a lot of hundreds. So I was waiting, I was very patient about it. But when the mid-off came up, I was like, this is the right opportunity. I might take it.

Pant scored another entertaining hundred. AK47 did quite well as a nightwatchman and Jurel took it deep to help India get the lead past 350. India now need 8 wickets. Nothing in this pitch as of now for the pacers. They have to force the issue, like Prasidh did - with his bowling and sledging with Rachin. The ball isn't really flying through so the fast bowlers will have to rest well and bend their backs to somehow get life out of this pitch. Washi bowled pretty well as well and he will hope there's more help for him tomorrow. New Zealand still 233 adrift so this game is out of their hands. Can India put on a stunning show with the ball and steal a win here? Or will it be a dull draw? Some key WTC points up for grabs tomorrow. We'll be back again in the morning for all the Day 5 stories. Good night!

Washington Sundar to Devon Conway, out Caught by Rishabh Pant!! Good catch and that's the end of Devon Conway who walks off shaking his head. Rishabh Pant wanted Washington Sundar to bowl into whatever rough that was there and then also said he can go a bit wider. Nice drift in, lands on a good length on off, Conway gets forward to defend, angled bat and it catches the thick inside edge. Hits the front pad (may have flicked the back thigh pad as well) and Pant is alert to take it to his left with both hands. Not easy to spot the inside edge and react, but Pant was watching all along.
